:_mod-docs-content-type: CONCEPT

[id="model-catalog-governance-overview_{context}"]
= Model catalog governance

[role='_abstract']
You can enforce organizational policies on AI model usage by controlling which models are visible and available in the model catalog.
Model catalog governance helps you meet compliance, security, regulatory, and intellectual property requirements by preventing unapproved or high-risk models from being discoverable by non-administrator users.

In regulated industries such as financial services, healthcare, and government, organizations must restrict end-user access to third-party models that have not been approved for internal use.
Model catalog governance provides the controls to enforce these policies at the platform level, so that data scientists and developers only see models that your organization has approved.

[id="how-disallow-listing-works_{context}"]
== How disallow-listing works

Disallow-listing removes a model from the catalog for non-administrator users.
When you disallow-list a model, the catalog service filters results before returning them to non-administrator users.

The following behavior occurs:

* Non-administrator users no longer see the model when browsing the catalog.
* If a non-administrator user accesses a disallow-listed model through a direct link or API query, they receive the message "Model is disabled by your administrator".
* Administrator users can still see and access disallow-listed models in the catalog.
* Disallow-listing does not affect running services or model instances that are already deployed.
Only the visibility and availability of the model in the catalog are changed.

Governance rules are stored as part of the catalog configuration and are managed through the AI Catalog Settings page in the {productname-short} dashboard.
You can re-enable a disallow-listed model at any time to restore its visibility to all users.

[id="disallow-listing-compared-to-source-level-filtering_{context}"]
== Disallow-listing compared to source-level filtering

{productname-short} provides two complementary levels of governance for the model catalog:

Disallow-listing individual models::
Hides specific models from non-administrator users across all catalog sources.
Use disallow-listing when you need to block individual models regardless of their source.

Source-level include and exclude filters::
Controls which models from a specific catalog source appear in the catalog.
Use source-level filters when you want to limit the models available from a particular Hugging Face organization or YAML source.

You can use both approaches together.
For example, you can use source-level filters to include only a subset of models from a large Hugging Face organization.
You can then disallow-list specific models from any source that violate your organizational policies.

[NOTE]
====
The model identifier format for disallow-listing depends on the source type.
For models from YAML-file sources, use the full `__organization__/__model-name__` format.
For models from Hugging Face sources, use only the `__model-name__` format.
For more information about the differences, see xref:model-catalog-source-types_{context}[Model catalog source types].
====

[id="role-based-access-control-for-governance-settings_{context}"]
== Role-based access control for governance settings

Only users with the Cluster Admin or {productname-short} Admin role can access the AI Catalog Settings page in the {productname-short} dashboard.
This page has both the model catalog source management controls and the disallow-list interface.

Regular users and data scientists cannot view or change governance settings.
If a non-administrator user needs access to a disallow-listed model, they must contact their {productname-short} administrator.

The following table summarizes the governance permissions by role.

.Governance permissions by role
[cols="1,1,1", options="header"]
|===
|Role
|Governance access
|Model visibility

|Cluster Admin
|Full access to governance settings and disallow list
|Can see all models, including disallow-listed models

|{productname-short} Admin
|Full access to governance settings and disallow list
|Can see all models, including disallow-listed models

|Non-administrator users
|No access to governance settings
|Cannot see disallow-listed models in the catalog
|===
